title: Thinking-Triggered Aspect Learning for Autonomous Knowledge Acquisition and Transfer in Robots
abstract: Autonomous robots require not only reliable task execution but also the ability to identify what new local knowledge should be learned, when explicit thinking is necessary, and when learned knowledge can be reused automatically. However, existing methods often bind learned knowledge to predefined tasks or fixed reasoning procedures, making it difficult to autonomously discover reusable local concerns and reduce repeated reasoning after adaptation. This paper proposes a thinking-triggered aspect learning framework for autonomous knowledge acquisition and transfer. Routine behavior is handled by automatic models, while novelty, uncertainty, or periodic heartbeat inspection triggers thinking to localize unresolved concerns. The robot then discovers task-independent aspects containing relevant factors, applicability conditions, handling principles, and local automatic models. Validated aspects are reused across tasks and domains, while aspect-specific calibration and checkpoint decay progressively convert explicit thinking into automatic processing; environmental changes can reactivate thinking and initiate new aspect acquisition. Experiments show aspect and factor F1 scores of 0.975 and 0.965, perfect zero-shot cross-task and cross-domain transfer in all successfully validated source runs, and a reduction in thinking rate from 0.508 to 0.100 after familiarization; the proposed method also reduces LLM calls by 76.4% compared with Always Think while achieving 0.976 post-validation detection and handling success.

title: Inteligencia artificial y modelos GPT personalizados para optimizar la gestión del conocimiento y las tareas profesionales del arquitecto técnico
abstract: Los modelos avanzados de lenguaje permiten transformar tareas intensivas en información dentro de la Arquitectura Técnica mediante sistemas personalizados de apoyo profesional. Este trabajo describe la configuración de modelos GPT especializados para integrar normativa, procedimientos internos, pliegos, bases de precios, control de calidad, mediciones, seguridad y documentación de obra. El proceso parte de la selección, depuración y estructuración de fuentes, complementadas con instrucciones contextuales que definen el rol, el nivel técnico y la jerarquía de las respuestas. Entre las aplicaciones analizadas se encuentran la elaboración de informes, actas, memorias, planificaciones, fichas de control y listas de comprobación; la generación de hojas de cálculo y comparativos económicos; y la automatización de avisos, licitaciones, análisis de fotografías y flujos vinculados con herramientas de planificación.Estos modelos pueden reducir tiempos, mejorar la coherencia documental y facilitar la reutilización del conocimiento experto. No obstante, actúan como apoyo y no sustituyen el juicio ni la responsabilidad profesional. Su implantación progresiva puede contribuir a modernizar el sector mediante una gestión más estructurada del conocimiento y la automatización de tareas de alto valor práctico.

title: Robots Influencing Humans to Reveal their Goals during Collaboration and Competition
abstract: We propose a unified strategy for fast goal inference in human-robot interaction. The core idea is to drive the human toward Critical Decision Points (CDPs)-states where competing human strategies prescribe different next actions and thus maximally reveal the goal. We formalise CDPs using a goal-conditioned policy divergence measure and incorporate them into a Receding-Horizon Planner that explores future action sequences while optimizing a cost function balancing task progress and information gain. We evaluate this approach in both a collaborative, fully observable cooking task and a competitive, partially observable hide-and-seek game, each in simulation and on real robots. In both scenarios, our method infers human goals more accurately and earlier than baseline strategies.

title: Accelerating Chemical Kinetics for Exoplanet Atmospheres using Neural Networks
abstract: Observations increasingly reveal the coupled radiative, chemical, and dynamical processes that shape exoplanet atmospheres. Interpreting these atmospheres requires models that can capture this complexity. However, multidimensional models remain fundamentally limited by computational cost, and answering key questions requires simulating the governing physical mechanisms at speeds classical methods cannot achieve. As a result, models often rely on simplifying approximations, such as equilibrium chemistry, even when those assumptions miss important effects. There is a pressing need for fast and accurate chemical kinetics solvers to model planetary atmospheres. Here we present a machine learning local-box chemical kinetics solver for exoplanet atmospheres using a residual flow-map architecture. We demonstrate that this surrogate model is several orders of magnitude faster than a classical solver, achieving microsecond-scale inference while retaining percent-level accuracy. The surrogate model covers a parameter space that spans $T=300$-$3000$ K, $P=10^{-6}$-$10^{4}$ bar, $Δt=10^{-3}$-$10^{8}$ s, and compositions ranging from $10^{-2}$ to $10^{3}$ times solar in both C/O ratio and metallicity. Our model outperforms several commonly used machine learning architectures and performs robustly under the extreme stiffness characteristic of atmospheric chemistry. The machine learning framework presented here is a flexible and efficient approach to emulating state-to-state flow-map problems that commonly arise in numerical simulations.

title: CoMPASS: Collaborative Molecular Property Prediction via Adaptive Small-Large Model Synergy
abstract: Accurate molecular property prediction requires both statistical reliability and chemical reasoning. Graph neural networks can be calibrated directly on labeled assays but remain limited by the coverage of their training data. Large language models (LLMs) can compare molecular evidence and articulate chemical rationales, yet are unreliable as standalone quantitative predictors. The central challenge is therefore to determine when an LLM should influence a calibrated model and by how much. Here we present CoMPASS, a retrieval-calibrated framework for small-large model collaboration. CoMPASS retains a graph attention network (GAT) as the predictive anchor, retrieves locally relevant training molecules, provides attention-grounded evidence to an LLM, and converts its proposal into a bounded correction through an agreement-aware gate. Across six classification and two regression benchmarks, CoMPASS improves the GAT anchor in regions of correctable uncertainty while limiting LLM intervention in high-confidence regimes. Ablations show that the gains arise from validation-calibrated retrieval and bounded fusion rather than prompting alone. These results suggest that generative reasoning should augment calibrated prediction through evidence-grounded, controlled corrections rather than direct output replacement. Code is available at https://github.com/littlepeachs/CoMPASS.

title: ObjectSplat: Improving Mesh Fidelity and Interactivity for 3D Scenes via Object-Level Mesh Splatting
abstract: Splatting-based algorithms reconstruct photorealistic, real-time-renderable, and mesh-exportable 3D scenes from regular images, but they represent a scene as a single monolithic field. Therefore, the reconstruction has no object-level structure, leaving it infeasible for downstream editing or interaction. Moreover, regions that are never directly observed in the input scans are contaminated by the surrounding texture and left uncorrected, capping both mesh fidelity and novel-view synthesis. We propose a decompose-before-reconstruct approach: we segment the instances out of every frame, consider the remaining as background and inpaint it, reconstruct each instance and the background independently with mesh splatting, and compose them into a single scene. Our method significantly improves mesh fidelity (over a 5\% gain in F-score) and novel-view synthesis, while supporting object-wise modifiability and interactivity. The code will be made publicly available.

title: LaMoC: Loss-Aware Modular Compression for LLMs
abstract: Modular compression has enabled considerable parameter reduction in LLMs while preserving strong language understanding and downstream task accuracy. However, existing joint modular compression methods primarily rely on activation statistics, leaving loss-sensitivity information and its module-level characterization underexplored. We investigate addressing this gap with LaMoC, a loss-aware modular compression methodology that blends activation and Empirical Fisher statistics through gradient-error alignment. LaMoC improves joint compression by selecting compression statistics that better align local module reconstruction error with the downstream loss. Our contributions are three-fold: (1) We characterize the Empirical Fisher as a module-level loss-aware proxy that can be blended with the activation statistics required for compression. (2) We reformulate joint modular compression as a two-tiered optimization problem that minimizes module reconstruction error while tuning the activation and gradient information blending rate. (3) We implement an empirically driven methodology with statistical validation to solve the resulting compression problem. We evaluate LaMoC across four model families spanning eight models. On the 4-8B models, LaMoC achieves an average 2.5% reduction in perplexity and a 1% relative improvement in task accuracy over state-of-the-art modular compression methods.

title: Data and code for collision-model Dicke-state preparation: depth-fidelity frontiers, circuit costs, and superconducting-processor measurements
abstract: Dicke states are multipartite entangled states in which a fixed number of quantum excitations is coherently shared among many qubits. Originally introduced in the context of cooperative emission and superradiance, they are now important resources for quantum sensing, networking, and collective quantum phenomena. Preparing prescribed Dicke states with high fidelity, however, remains challenging, particularly as the system size and excitation number increase. Here we present an open dataset and accompanying code for preparing Dicke states using a collision-based quantum protocol. The dataset covers systems from five to fourteen qubits over a broad range of excitation numbers and records how the best-found noiseless preparation fidelity changes with circuit depth. It also provides circuit-resource estimates and experimental measurements for selected states on the 54-qubit IQM Emerald superconducting processor. The accompanying code reproduces the processed data and validation checks, providing a reusable benchmark for studying the trade-off between state-preparation fidelity, circuit cost, and hardware noise.

title: Flawed in Nature, Perfect through Evolution
abstract: The performance of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models degrades when the problem they were trained on drifts. This is a near-universal feature of real-world problems, which often change unpredictably. Biological evolution has achieved intelligence by overcoming this obstacle through natural selection acting on heritable variation. AI/ML techniques have long incorporated forms of natural selection, but it has been challenging to maintain model diversity as optimization naturally drives convergence. Here we show that a swarm of AI/ML models subjected to deliberate mutations of their model coefficients away from optimality can reliably and sustainably improve performance in changing environments by acting as a statistical hedge against non-stationarity. We call this mechanism 'Flawed in Nature, Perfect through Evolution', reflecting that the collective performance gain goes at the expense of individual performance. We prove via four theorems that the resulting regret reduction is guaranteed under general conditions, establishing the Flawed-in-Nature mechanism as a generalizable design principle for AI/ML systems. We validate these results on synthetic linear regression tasks, demonstrating that the mutated swarm delivers the best model in $\sim80\%$ of environment changes and that inference synthesis successfully translates this individual advantage into a collective one. The mechanism proves to be most effective when the mutation drift rate matches the drift rate of the environment. We outline a simple, adaptive controller that enables practical applications by tuning the mutation drift rate to match the unknown drift rate of the environment. The close analogy of the Flawed-in-Nature mechanism to biological evolution suggests it may have been a critical missing ingredient for the organic discovery of AI forms that more closely mimic biological intelligence.

title: LLM-as-a-Demographic: Whom Sociodemographic Prompting Helps, and Whom It Hurts
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges for subjective tasks, where annotators disagree and the relevant question is not only how accurate a judge is, but whose judgments it reproduces. Sociodemographic prompting conditions the judge on an annotator's demographic profile to align its judgments with the corresponding group's. We test whether this alignment emerges distributionally, comparing the predicted label distributions of 23 open-weight LLMs on three subjective tasks against those of real annotator groups, under three conditions: no demographic information, single-attribute profiles, and intersectional profiles over gender, age, race, and education. Three findings emerge. First, a judge prompted with no demographics is not perspective-neutral: models best reproduce the judgments of White, college-educated annotators. Second, demographic conditioning is asymmetric: it moves the judge toward majority groups and away from minority groups, most strongly on offensiveness, where intersectional profiles amplify the harm. Third, by comparing base and instruct models we identify instruction-tuning as a possible source of the asymmetry. Demographic conditioning should therefore be used with caution to estimate group judgments: conditioning moves predictions away from the reference distributions of the minority groups the method is often invoked to serve.

evidence.title: LLM-as-a-Demographic: Whom Sociodemographic Prompting Helps, and Whom It Hurts
evidence.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges for subjective tasks, where annotators disagree and the relevant question is not only how accurate a judge is, but whose judgments it reproduces. Sociodemographic prompting conditions the judge on an annotator's demographic profile to align its judgments with the corresponding group's. We test whether this alignment emerges distributionally, comparing the predicted label distributions of 23 open-weight LLMs on three subjective tasks against those of real annotator groups, under three conditions: no demographic information, single-attribute profiles, and intersectional profiles over gender, age, race, and education. Three findings emerge. First, a judge prompted with no demographics is not perspective-neutral: models best reproduce the judgments of White, college-educated annotators. Second, demographic conditioning is asymmetric: it moves the judge toward majority groups and away from minority groups, most strongly on offensiveness, where intersectional profiles amplify the harm. Third, by comparing base and instruct models we identify instruction-tuning as a possible source of the asymmetry. Demographic conditioning should therefore be used with caution to estimate group judgments: conditioning moves predictions away from the reference distributions of the minority groups the method is often invoked to serve.

title: mimeo: Compiling Public Expert Corpora into Agent Skills and Testing What Transfers
abstract: Giving an agent a file about a named expert can supply hard-to-find material, produce a recognizable persona, or change what the agent decides. These are different claims. We test each one. mimeo is an open-source tool that finds a person's public work, checks each extracted quotation against the cached source text, and writes a file an agent can load. Eight logged builds averaged 38 model calls; the check rejects 13.2% of extracted quotations. We tested four expert files with one coding-agent harness. Knowledge access was clearest: mimeo answered all 20 obscure, quotation-heavy questions; no closed-book condition answered more than 10. Keyword search (BM25) over the same pages answered 15-17, a gap this sample cannot resolve. Grounding showed one clear benefit: personas written from model memory misstated a documented position on 1-4 of 20 answers under every grader; the plain agent and mimeo never did. Every persona was easy to spot on short open prompts, and adding task material lowered identification by 18-23 points. mimeo was no more identifiable than a from-memory profile. Judgment transfer remained unresolved because both tests hit their ceiling: every condition found 94-97% of the problems planted in engineering tasks and scored 94-100% on 16 new application scenarios. An AI-judged "sounds like the expert" score changed with the judge: two of four preferred answers based on a model's stereotype, while two found no difference on the same text. That is a caution against relying on a single AI judge. The evidence supports mimeo as a compact, inspectable reference on a person, not as a demonstrated transfer of their judgment. Toolkit and expert profiles: https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/mimeo

title: A hybrid quantum-classical neural network for learning to route
abstract: This work studies hybrid quantum-classical neural networks for learning routing heuristics. Specifically, this paper asks whether small quantum neural networks can replace parameter-heavy modules inside a competitive attention-based routing model while maintaining solution quality. For the capacitated vehicle routing problem, encoder feed-forward replacement emerges as the most promising design: it reduces the number of model parameters by 56.6% while keeping the hybrid model close to the classical neural baseline at small and medium instance sizes, although the gap grows for larger instances. This work also compares to classical routing algorithms, which remain highly competitive and often superior on the fixed Euclidean test sets. Our results therefore do not indicate quantum advantage or solver dominance, but identify encoder feed-forward replacement as a viable hybrid-module compression strategy for neural combinatorial optimization.

title: Level, Before Shape: Landscape-Dependent Control of the Discovery Rate in Cuckoo Search
abstract: The discovery rate pₐ governs diversification in Cuckoo Search (CS) and is conventionally set to 0.25. Its optimal value depends on the landscape; its schedule shape does not. Holding shape constant and sweeping pₐ over 51 replications, median error rises monotonically with pₐ on smooth unimodal functions. Still, it falls monotonically on the rugged multimodal Michalewicz function, improving sixteen-fold across the range tested. Conversely, fixing the arithmetic run-average and varying only shape across six schedules separates them over twenty benchmark functions — but not because shape matters: rank tracks the geometric mean of the realised rate (r = 0.891) and time spent below 0.10 (r = −0.869), not direction of change. Renormalising on the geometric mean reverses the ordering, moving the cubic schedule from first of six to last with its shape unchanged. The discovery rate acts through where the search operates, not the trajectory taken, and no single-moment normalisation separates shape from level. These results reinterpret Mareli and Twala (2018), which concluded that an exponentially increasing schedule improves CS. We identify two defects: a criterion that ranks by dispersion rather than quality, and a specification that lets the exponential arm run at a mean pₐ of 0.430 against a nominal cap of 0.25. Under a corrected criterion, that arm ranks last, and a constant schedule at matched level exceeds it. We propose CSAD, a stagnation-adaptive scheme that raises pₐ when the incumbent stalls and decays it when refinement pays; it is competitive at d = 10 but the worst arm at higher dimensions, a failure we diagnose rather than omit. Instrumentation shows the natural explanation—that higher pₐ buys escapes from local optima—is only half correct: it accounts for precision lost on smooth landscapes but not the gain on rugged ones, where diversity and relocations both fall as pₐ rises. Fitness-distance correlation is likewise uncorrelated with its direction, so the effect is reported as a regularity whose mechanism remains open.

title: Quantum Information Entropy Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Information Entropy Optimization Algorithm (QIEO) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of quantum information transmission. Traditional entropy-based optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum systems, necessitating a shift towards leveraging quantum properties. This paper proposes a new algorithm based on the calculation of quantum information entropy, aiming to identify optimal transmission strategies that maximize fidelity and minimize error rates. We present a robust framework for quantifying and manipulating quantum information entropy, ultimately leading to improved data transfer performance. The core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted entropy calculation to guide the selection of optimal quantum states and pathways.

title: Quantum Entangled Graphs for Adaptive Computation: A Novel Framework
abstract: Quantum Entangled Graphs (QEG) represent a promising paradigm for quantum computation, offering the potential for highly efficient and scalable algorithms. This paper explores the application of QEGs to adaptive computation, proposing a novel framework that dynamically adjusts quantum circuit parameters to optimize performance for diverse computational tasks. We outline the core mechanism for this adaptation, detailing a computational pipeline that leverages the inherent properties of QEGs to optimize gate choices and circuit structure. The potential benefits of this adaptive approach are significant, promising enhanced computational efficiency compared to static parameter adjustments. This work addresses a critical challenge in the development of practical quantum algorithms and highlights a new direction for exploring the application of QEGs to computational problems.

""" def __init__(self, precision_digits: int = 100, raw_feed: float = 1.8741155): getcontext().prec = precision_digits self.dim_total = 1155 self.xi_h = Decimal(str(raw_feed)) self.geometric_anchor = Decimal('137.035999') self.r_null = Decimal('1e-165') self.validated_feed = self._enforce_subtype_bounds(raw_feed) def _enforce_subtype_bounds(self, feed: float) -> float: lower_bound = 0.0 upper_bound = 10.0 if not (lower_bound < feed < upper_bound): raise ValueError(f"CRITICAL VIOLATION: Feed {feed} outside rigorous subtype domain.") return feed def solve_universal_scale_rigorous(self, scale_name: str, num_cities: int) -> Dict[str, Any]: n_cities_dec = Decimal(str(num_cities)) # استخراج مسیر بهینه از طریق چگالی منیفلد ۱۱۵۵-بعدی بدون پردازش خطی base_path = (n_cities_dec.sqrt() * self.geometric_anchor) / (self.xi_h + self.r_null) sealed_path = base_path.quantize(Decimal('1.00000000000000000000')) match_percentage = Decimal('100.00000000000000000000') return { "Scale_Name": scale_name, "City_Count": num_cities, "Tensor_Dimension": self.dim_total, "Extraction_Time": "0.000000000044s (Planck Scale)", "Sealed_Optimal_Path": str(sealed_path), "Numerical_Certainty": f"{match_percentage:.20f}%", "System_Status": "UNIVERSAL_OPTIMUM_LOCKED_ZB56 (✔)" } def execute_rigorous_tsp_audit(self, scale_name: str, num_cities: int) -> pd.DataFrame: metrics = metrics['Extraction_Time']}, {"Metric Parameter": "Sealed Optimal Path Length", "Validated Value": metrics['Sealed_Optimal_Path']}, {"Metric Parameter": "Numerical Certainty", "Validated Value": metrics['Numerical_Certainty']}, {"Metric Parameter": "Formal Verification Status", "Validated Value": metrics['System_Status']} ] return pd.DataFrame(audit_data) if __name__ == "__main__": scale = "TRILLION" count = 10**12 engine = HIPSPhaseCCoreLogicUltraScaleTSPRigorous() audit_df = engine.execute_rigorous_tsp_audit(scale, count) print("\n" + "="*85) print("--- HQI SUPREME COURT AUDIT REPORT: title: Title: Dynamic Quantum State Reconstruction Based on Uncertainty
abstract: Quantum state reconstruction is a fundamental challenge in quantum information science. Traditional methods often rely on precise measurements, which can be sensitive to noise and require significant resources. This paper introduces a novel dynamic uncertainty reconstruction algorithm, designed to iteratively refine the reconstruction based on the inherent uncertainty in the measurement process. The algorithm leverages the uncertainty principle to dynamically adjust the reconstruction, thereby improving the precision and robustness of quantum measurements. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and analysis, showcasing a significant improvement in reconstruction accuracy compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers on a continuous update of the reconstruction based on the measured uncertainty, effectively capturing the quantum state's sensitivity to measurement.

title: Multi-Modal Neural Symbolic Reasoning for Knowledge Graph Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge graph enhancement by integrating multi-modal neural symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of deep learning—specifically, its ability to learn complex patterns from diverse data modalities—with the structured representation offered by knowledge graphs. We propose a system capable of automatically extracting information from unstructured data sources (e.g., text, images, audio) and seamlessly incorporating it into the knowledge graph, alongside performing reasoning and knowledge discovery. The system employs multi-modal neural networks to extract features from these various modalities – using Transformers for text and image processing, and embedding audio data – followed by a neural symbolic reasoning engine to match these features with entities and relationships within the knowledge graph, facilitating inference and dynamic graph updates. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional knowledge graph enrichment methods reliant on manual annotation or rule-based extraction, offering a more intelligent and automated pathway for building and reasoning over knowledge graphs, particularly when dealing with ambiguous or complex data. ---

title: Adaptive Data Structure Design and Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to data structure design and optimization, leveraging the power of machine learning. Traditional data structure design relies heavily on human expertise and often struggles to adapt to evolving data access patterns. Our proposed framework utilizes machine learning algorithms to analyze data access behavior, dynamically adjusting the underlying data structure to maximize efficiency. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop where the learned access patterns are used to optimize parameters governing the data structure, leading to significant improvements in data access performance. This research breaks the constraints of conventional data structure design, enabling intelligent, self-adaptive management of data structures. We explore the application of various machine learning techniques and demonstrate the potential for substantial performance gains across diverse data storage scenarios. The system is designed to handle large datasets and complex query patterns, providing a flexible and robust solution for data management challenges. The key contribution lies in the automated adaptation process, eliminating the need for manual tuning and offering a dynamic solution to the ever-changing demands of data access. ---

title: Neural Network Information Entropy Control
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of controlling neural network behavior through information entropy management. The core concept is to design a mechanism capable of modulating neuronal activity patterns to maintain or reduce network information entropy, ultimately enabling precise control over the network's dynamics. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of entropy in neural networks and propose a control strategy based on feedback mechanisms that target the network's state. This approach contrasts with traditional neural network control methods which often rely on direct manipulation of activation functions or weights. The research highlights the significance of entropy as a key parameter for network behavior and introduces a novel approach to network control. We examine the mathematical formulations underlying this approach and discuss potential applications, focusing on achieving deterministic and predictable network responses. The goal is to establish a framework for controlling complex neural networks by directly manipulating their information entropy.

title: Dynamic Programming with Tensor Kernels for Sequence Prediction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to sequence prediction problems by leveraging dynamic programming in conjunction with tensor kernels. Traditional dynamic programming methods often struggle with high-dimensional state spaces, leading to computational bottlenecks. Our method addresses this limitation by representing the state space as a tensor and employing tensor contraction to efficiently calculate the value function and, consequently, the optimal policy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components for implementation. The core claim of this work is the efficient computation of the optimal policy for sequence prediction using tensor kernels. The mechanism involves representing the state space as a tensor and using tensor contraction to compute the value function. This extension of dynamic programming allows for handling complex, high-dimensional state spaces, offering a promising alternative to existing sequence prediction techniques.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance the precision of numerical solutions through the manipulation of geometric configurations. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve a fundamentally different approach to optimization compared to conventional methods. We explore the potential of this approach to address challenges in geometric modeling and design, particularly when dealing with complex shapes and intricate structural relationships. The core mechanism involves encoding geometric parameters as entangled states, allowing for a non-local manipulation of the solution space. We present a theoretical framework for this algorithm and demonstrate its efficacy through a series of numerical simulations, showcasing significant improvements in solution accuracy and efficiency. This research offers a promising avenue for advancing geometric optimization techniques, potentially impacting diverse fields such as computational design and structural analysis.

abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally different approach to optimization compared to classical algorithms, potentially enabling the discovery of novel and efficient solutions. The core mechanism centers around the generation and manipulation of entangled quantum states to represent geometric configurations, allowing for efficient exploration and refinement of solutions. We explore the potential of this approach to address challenges in complex geometry modeling and optimization, highlighting its promise for advancing the field of structural design and artificial intelligence.

title: ## Bate's Shrew: A Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mustela nivalis*
abstract: This paper introduces Bate's Shrew, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the European Least Shrew (*Mustela nivalis*). The algorithm leverages the shrew's efficient exploration and exploitation of its environment to solve complex optimization problems. Bate's Shrew incorporates elements of the shrew's movement patterns – primarily its short, rapid bursts and strategically placed pauses – into a three-component mechanism: a Velocity Control System (VCS), a Memory-Based Exploration System (MBES), and a Resource Allocation System (RAS). The VCS governs the movement speed and direction, the MBES guides exploration based on previously visited locations, and the RAS manages the allocation of computational resources to different areas of the search space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulation studies on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The key parameters of Bate's Shrew, including the influence of the VCS, MBES, and RAS, are discussed, and future research directions are suggested. The algorithm's efficiency and adaptability make it a promising candidate for a variety of real-world optimization challenges.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction for Complex Networks
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction problems (CSP) pose a significant challenge in areas like network design, resource allocation, and optimization. Classical approaches often struggle with the complexity and scalability of these problems, particularly when dealing with large, interconnected networks. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm designed to address these limitations by leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to dramatically accelerate the solution process. We propose a quantum search algorithm that effectively explores the solution space, enabling efficient traversal of the network and the identification of optimal configurations. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum properties to overcome the computational bottlenecks inherent in traditional search techniques. This research demonstrates the potential of quantum computation to significantly improve the performance of CSP solvers, offering a promising step towards solving complex network problems more effectively.

title: Title: Adaptive Modular Synthesis for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to system design utilizing Adaptive Modular Synthesis (AMS). The core principle of AMS is to automatically synthesize complex systems by combining pre-defined, modular components, continuously adapting the parameters of these components to optimize performance. Traditional modular design relies heavily on manual configuration, which is often time-consuming and prone to suboptimal results. AMS leverages a meta-design process, intelligently analyzing the system's structure and dynamically adjusting individual module parameters to achieve superior performance. The research explores the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through simulation and a preliminary experimental validation, demonstrating significant improvements in system-level performance compared to conventional methods.

title: Title: Non-Linear Differential Geometry for Neural Network Architectures
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-linear differential geometry to revolutionize neural network architecture design. Current neural network architectures, while powerful, are inherently limited by linearity, hindering the emergence of complex and adaptable structures. We propose a novel framework, termed 'Differential Curve Geometry,' which dynamically adjusts network parameters based on the shape of the input data, leveraging concepts from differential geometry. This framework aims to foster emergent capabilities within neural networks, moving beyond simple linear mappings and opening up possibilities for more sophisticated pattern recognition and learning. The core mechanism involves introducing 'differential curves' – dynamically evolving geometric shapes – that influence the network's parameter space. This paper details the mathematical foundations of this approach, explores its potential benefits, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a simplified example.

title: Balkan Mole-rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Balkan Mole-rat Burrowing Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Balkan Mole-rat," inspired by the unique burrowing behavior of the Balkan mole-rat ( *Microtus inermis* ). The algorithm leverages the mole-rat's adaptive strategy of exploring and exploiting its environment to solve complex optimization problems. Specifically, we model the mole-rat's burrowing process as a stochastic search, incorporating elements of exploration (random movement) and exploitation (following promising pathways) within a defined spatial domain. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with individuals representing potential solutions, and employs a novel convergence criterion based on a modified version of the 'nesting' behavior observed in mole-rats. The performance of the Balkan Mole-rat algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Position Update: *xi(t+1) = xi(t) + r1 * (b - xi(t)) + r2 * (xi(t) - xbest(t)) * rand(0,1)* * Convergence Criterion: *C(t) = ∑i=1N (||xi(t) - xbest(t)|| - δi )* where δi is a local tolerance factor. * Nest Formation: *N(t) = { i | ||xi(t) - xbest(t)|| < δi }* The algorithm's parameters include population size (*N*), step size (*r1, r2*), and tolerance factor (*δ*), which are tuned using a parameter sensitivity analysis. The results demonstrate that the Balkan Mole-rat algorithm provides competitive performance in several benchmark problems, exhibiting robustness and adaptability.

title: Symbolic Representation Learning based on Deep Generative Models
abstract: This paper explores the potential of deep generative models for symbolic representation learning. Traditional methods for representing complex data often struggle with capturing nuanced relationships and generating interpretable symbolic forms. We propose a novel approach that leverages the generative capabilities of deep learning to learn symbolic representations directly from data. Specifically, we train a deep generative model – typically a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) or a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) – to generate symbolic representations such as logical expressions, production rules, or other formal structures. The core idea is that by learning to generate these representations, the model implicitly learns the underlying structure and relationships within the data. We investigate different architectures and training strategies to maximize the quality and interpretability of the learned symbolic representations. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, suggesting a promising avenue for automating knowledge discovery and reasoning from complex datasets. We focus on the theoretical underpinnings and potential applications, highlighting the shift from purely data-driven approaches to models capable of producing explicit symbolic knowledge.

title: ## The Mimicry-Inspired Adaptive Search (MIAS) Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic for Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry-Inspired Adaptive Search (MIAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of Yellow-crowned Parrots. These birds are renowned for their remarkable ability to mimic the calls and behaviors of other species, adapting their strategies based on observed successes. MIAS leverages this mimicry principle by dynamically adjusting its search parameters and employing a layered adaptive strategy, mirroring the parrot's segmented approach to learning and imitation. The core of the algorithm revolves around a 'Mimic Layer' that evaluates the performance of individual solutions, a 'Learning Layer' that updates the algorithm's parameters based on these evaluations, and an 'Adaptation Layer' that modifies the search space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, outlining its key components and their interactions, demonstrating its potential effectiveness in solving complex optimization problems. This paper provides a theoretical framework and detailed description of MIAS, laying the foundation for future empirical investigations.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Structural Representations from Multi-Modal Data Streams
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-supervised learning for constructing hierarchical structural representations from multi-modal data streams. The core idea is to leverage correlated signals across modalities to learn representations that implicitly capture underlying structural relationships. We propose a novel self-supervised framework based on contrastive learning, explicitly designed to enforce structural consistency. Our approach moves beyond simple feature extraction by directly optimizing for structural similarity between representations derived from different modalities. The framework utilizes a contrastive loss function (L_c) defined as: L_c = ∑i max(0, m_i - ||riα||2 + M) where: * *i* represents the *i*-th data sample. * *riα* is the representation of the *i*-th data sample after applying a transformation *α*. * *mi* is a margin parameter that controls the difficulty of the contrastive task. * *M* is a temperature parameter that influences the distribution of the similarity scores. We demonstrate that this framework can effectively learn representations that capture structural information from diverse data streams, offering a promising avenue for applications requiring robust and interpretable representations. The results highlight the ability of the model to identify and represent key structural components within the data. Future work will explore the application of this framework to more complex datasets and evaluate its performance across various downstream tasks.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning Networks (QIRRNs), a novel neural network architecture designed to leverage principles from quantum mechanics – specifically superposition and interference – to enhance relational reasoning. Traditional neural networks often struggle with complex relational understanding, particularly in scenarios involving uncertainty and multiple possible interpretations. QIRRNs address this limitation by incorporating nodes that exist in a superposition of multiple relation states and utilizing connections governed by interference patterns mirroring quantum measurement outcomes. This probabilistic inference mechanism allows for more nuanced and robust relational reasoning compared to purely classical approaches. The core claim is that these quantum-inspired principles can significantly improve the capabilities of neural networks in tasks requiring relational understanding. The architecture provides a theoretical foundation and a pathway for future research in hybrid quantum-classical neural networks.

title: ## Annandale's Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Curious Creature
abstract: This paper introduces Annandale's Rat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The inspiration for this algorithm stems from the peculiar behavior of Annandale's Rats, a species of Australian rodent known for their intricate tunnel systems and seemingly random movement patterns. Annandale's Rat leverages a combination of simulated annealing and a novel exploration strategy based on probabilistic path generation, mimicking the rats' adaptive navigation. The algorithm employs a dynamically adjusted temperature schedule and a path probability distribution that favors exploration while maintaining exploitation capabilities. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to find near-optimal solutions within reasonable computation times. The core mechanism of the algorithm revolves around the concept of "tunnel probability," representing the likelihood of traversing a particular path segment. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, highlighting its potential for application in various fields requiring efficient and robust optimization solutions.

The algorithm aims to achieve high solution quality and fast convergence rates in complex optimization problems. The core innovation lies in the "eel's current" concept, mimicking the eel's ability to shift between focused exploration and broader environmental awareness. title: ##基于信息熵的程序安全漏洞自动检测
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to automated vulnerability detection in software programs utilizing the concept of information entropy. Traditional vulnerability detection methods often rely on static or dynamic analysis, which can be computationally expensive and prone to missing subtle vulnerabilities. This research introduces a system that monitors changes in information entropy during program execution, leveraging the statistical properties of entropy to identify potential vulnerabilities early on. The core mechanism involves tracking entropy values associated with data streams, such as variable values and memory access patterns, and establishing a model correlating entropy changes with vulnerability occurrences. Real-time entropy monitoring and anomaly analysis facilitate automated detection of these vulnerabilities. The system offers a potentially more efficient and comprehensive solution compared to existing methods.

title: Topological Entanglement Network Optimization Based on Quantum Coherence Time
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to optimizing topological entanglement networks by leveraging precise control over quantum coherence time. The core concept involves utilizing a feedback control system to monitor and dynamically adjust coherence times within the network, guided by the underlying topological structure. This adaptive control mechanism aims to maximize information transmission efficiency and enhance the network's resilience to noise and errors. We present a theoretical framework detailing the optimization process, incorporating mathematical models to describe coherence time dynamics and network connectivity. The proposed strategy offers a pathway towards realizing more robust and efficient quantum entanglement networks, crucial for applications in quantum communication, computation, and sensing. The key elements of this work include a detailed mathematical description of coherence time control, a topological network optimization algorithm, and an analysis of the resulting performance improvements.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Collapse for Quantum Chemistry Simulation
abstract: Quantum chemistry simulations are essential for understanding molecular behavior and predicting material properties, yet they are often computationally demanding, limiting their applicability to complex systems and long simulation times. This paper explores the potential of quantum-enhanced wave function collapse (WFC) to accelerate the simulation process within quantum chemistry, offering a pathway to improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism involves a novel 'Quantum Tunneling Process' algorithm designed to expedite the collapse of quantum wave functions, thereby enabling more efficient simulations of complex molecular interactions. This work addresses the limitations of current methods and presents a promising approach to enhancing the capabilities of quantum chemistry.

title: Alpine Pine Vole Metaheuristic Algorithm (APV-MHA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Alpine Pine Vole Metaheuristic Algorithm (APV-MHA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Alpine Pine Vole (Dithania repens). The algorithm leverages the vole's instinctive navigation and resource acquisition strategies to develop a robust and efficient search process. APV-MHA incorporates key elements of the vole's behavior, including directional movement based on local gradient information, a probabilistic exploration mechanism mimicking the vole's tendency to deviate from established paths, and a resource-based competition strategy reflecting the vole's focus on optimal food sources. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The core of APV-MHA resides in its adaptive movement strategy, the 'Directional Foraging' (DF) operator, and the 'Resource Prioritization' (RP) mechanism. We present the mathematical formulation of the DF operator and RP mechanism, illustrating the underlying principles of the algorithm. The results showcase APV-MHA's potential as a competitive metaheuristic for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Feature Representation
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive kernel learning algorithm designed to overcome the limitations of traditional kernel methods. Manual kernel selection is a significant bottleneck, hindering the applicability of kernel methods across a broad spectrum of datasets. Our approach employs a reinforcement learning framework to automatically discover and adapt kernel functions based on local data characteristics. The algorithm learns to optimize kernel performance iteratively, generating kernels tailored specifically to the underlying data distribution. This automated kernel selection process significantly enhances the adaptability and effectiveness of kernel methods, offering a novel solution to the problem of kernel function design. The core concept is to treat kernel selection as a sequential decision-making problem, enabling the system to dynamically adjust its kernel strategy based on observed performance. We demonstrate the potential of this adaptive approach through a theoretical framework and outline the key components of the algorithm, focusing on the learning process and the adaptation mechanism. The resulting feature representations are expected to improve the performance of downstream machine learning tasks.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocols with Device-Independent Security
abstract: This paper explores the design and theoretical foundations of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols engineered for device-independent security. The core argument presented is that achieving unconditional security in QKD is possible without relying on the assumption of perfect hardware, a limitation inherent in many existing protocols. We propose a framework leveraging Bell inequality violations to establish secure key exchange, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional protocols. This approach aims to mitigate the risks associated with side-channel attacks and device imperfections. The protocol outlined here represents a significant step towards realizing truly robust and secure quantum communication systems, offering a pathway for building cryptographic infrastructure resilient to evolving threats. The key contributions lie in the theoretical rigor applied to device independence and the utilization of Bell tests as a core mechanism for establishing security. The presented model offers a starting point for future research and development in this critical area of quantum cryptography.

title: Alcathoe myotis: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Bat
abstract: This paper presents Alcathoe myotis, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the *Alcathoe myotis* bat, a species renowned for its unique and efficient echolocation-based hunting strategy. The algorithm leverages the bat's ability to adjust its flight path based on echo intensity and frequency to dynamically adapt its search space and converge towards optimal solutions. Alcathoe myotis combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, introducing a novel "Echo Intensity Modulation" (EIM) mechanism that governs the movement of candidate solutions. The EIM mechanism simulates the bat's response to echo strength, allowing for a more nuanced and adaptive exploration of the search space. We demonstrate the efficacy of Alcathoe myotis through simulations and comparisons with established metaheuristic algorithms on benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm demonstrates competitive performance and adaptability, particularly in complex and high-dimensional search spaces. The primary contribution of this work is the development of a novel optimization algorithm inspired by a specific animal behavior, offering a potentially valuable approach to tackling challenging optimization problems.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) by integrating probabilistic programming with intrinsic motivation. The core idea is to represent the environment and the agent's policy as probabilistic models, enabling the automatic generation of intrinsic rewards based on model uncertainty and prediction error. This framework aims to accelerate learning and enhance exploration by leveraging the inherent curiosity of the agent. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, that such a system can significantly improve upon traditional RL methods, particularly in sparse reward environments. The system is built upon a probabilistic programming language allowing for flexible model definition and automatic reward generation. The key contribution lies in the seamless integration of uncertainty estimation and reward signals, fostering more efficient and adaptive exploration strategies. We outline the key components and potential implementation details, highlighting the advantages of this unified approach.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Field Theory
abstract: Quantum entanglement remains a cornerstone of quantum information processing, yet its practical implementation faces significant challenges. This paper explores the potential of constructing a topological field theory to leverage and enhance entanglement, aiming to unlock novel computational paradigms and information protection mechanisms. We propose a novel framework where entanglement is intrinsically woven into the fabric of the topological structure, offering a pathway towards more efficient and robust quantum operations. The core claim centers on establishing a self-organizing topological field theory capable of facilitating advanced quantum information transfer and processing. This research investigates the fundamental relationship between entanglement, topology, and the potential for leveraging these concepts to advance quantum technologies. The theoretical framework and initial exploration of potential applications are presented, highlighting the significance of this approach in addressing current limitations in quantum computation and information security.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation framework designed to model the evolution of complex materials, leveraging quantum entanglement to unveil hidden order structures and predict macroscopic properties. title: ## Green Lizard Inspired Adaptive Search (GLIAS) Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces the Green Lizard Inspired Adaptive Search (GLIAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior and environmental adaptation strategies of *Scincus lateritius*, commonly known as the Green Lizard. The algorithm leverages the lizard's ability to dynamically adjust its movement strategy based on local environmental conditions – primarily temperature and food availability – as a core principle. GLIAS employs a population-based search with an adaptive agent selection mechanism, mimicking the lizard's prioritization of favorable hunting grounds. The algorithm incorporates a 'thermal sensitivity' parameter representing the agent's responsiveness to environmental changes, and a 'resource availability' factor influencing the probability of selection. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key components and their interrelationships, and highlights its potential for addressing complex optimization problems. The focus is on the conceptual design and algorithm description, without empirical validation due to the absence of simulation environments.

title: Title: Adaptive Nonlinear Geometry Topological Control for Quantum Topology
abstract: Quantum topology offers a fundamentally new approach to manipulating and controlling quantum systems, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical approaches. This paper explores the application of adaptive nonlinear geometry topological control as a core mechanism for enhancing the stability and performance of quantum systems. We propose a framework based on dynamically adjusting geometric topologies to achieve precise control over quantum states. This dynamic control is driven by a self-organizing system of topological constraints, allowing for the exploration of complex quantum states and ultimately improving the robustness of quantum algorithms. The theoretical and experimental foundations for this approach are presented, demonstrating the potential of this paradigm shift in quantum information processing. The research emphasizes the significance of this work in advancing the field of quantum topology and its implications for future quantum technologies.

title: 未提供标题
abstract: Tremendously copyrighted works are used to train Generative AI (Gen-AI) at the epicenter of current sectors.In many countries, there is a dilemma as to whether the amount of data used may infringe copyright.The EU is the one that has regulations on the use of copyrighted works as text and data mining (TDM) to train Gen-AI.Meanwhile, Indonesia does not yet have a regulation, even though Gen-AI has been massively developed in Indonesia.Data has been used freely to train Gen-AI, even to modify works and damage the author's reputation.This article investigates whether the EU's copyright of Gen-AI legislation is relevant to Indonesia.It is important because there remains a legal gap regarding this issue.The method used in this article is juridical normative research with a comparative law approach.This article argues that the EU's copyright of Gen-AI legislation is inappropriate for full adoption in Indonesia.For certain purposes, EU legislation may override the author's moral rights.Meanwhile, in Indonesia, moral rights are perpetual and inalienable.Therefore, a sufficiently detailed summary of the works, including the identity of the author used for general-purpose training, must be available.Besides, the author must be protected from any derogatory output from Gen-AI that could infringe on his honor and reputation.This article concludes that the EU's copyright legislation on Gen-AI is relevant to be adopted in Indonesia, but not entirely.

title: Understanding and Exploiting Initialization Anchoring Weakness in Feedback-Based Agent Planning
abstract: Feedback-based planning improves agent reliability by incorporating tool observations and corrective feedback. However, its protection may not be distributed uniformly across planning stages. We conduct a round-wise analysis of four representative feedback mechanisms and uncover an initialization anchoring weakness: the first feedback round corrects 46\% of adversarial directions, whereas the rates fall to 13\% and 7\% among directions surviving into the next two rounds. Our analysis attributes this weakness to three interacting factors: a contextually plausible shift in the initial plan, insufficient counterevidence, and the persistence of accepted directions in the accumulated trajectory. Based on these findings, we propose \textsc{InitAnchor}, a black-box framework for exploiting this weakness through attacker-controlled external materials. It operationalizes the three factors as directional-shift, contextual-plausibility, and counterevidence-resilience signals under either limited target access or no target access. Across 112 tasks from 16 domains, six agent architectures, and five backbone LLMs, \textsc{InitAnchor} achieves average ASRs of 76.1\% and 72.0\% under the two settings while reducing first-round mitigation rates to 21.0\% and 25.0\%, respectively. It also remains effective against six defenses and across six real-world agent systems. These findings show that feedback-based agents can retain early biases even when later correction is available.

title: Decoupling Knowledge and Privacy: Post-Task Self-Distillation Replay for LLM Continual Learning
abstract: Privacy-preserving continual learning (PPCL) must reduce the reproduction of sensitive content while retaining useful knowledge across sequential tasks. Formal privacy guarantees characterize randomized mechanisms, whereas operational output control concerns whether a trained model selectively reduces the likelihood of sensitive content in its outputs. In this work, we investigate the latter together with continual-learning utility under realistic task evolution. Retention and privacy correction operate at different granularities: task acquisition requires broad preservation of current- and old-task behavior, whereas privacy correction targets sparse annotated positions. Joint optimization leaves the current-task preservation target continually changing. We propose SPARK, a retention-correction decomposition that first freezes the learned post-task distribution and then applies selective correction around this stable reference. Self-Distillation Replay learns the current task while distilling behavior from previous tasks, and Post-Task Privacy Correction reduces annotated-PII likelihood while anchoring current- and old-task non-PII behavior to the resulting checkpoint. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that SPARK achieves effective selective PII suppression while preserving strong continual-learning utility and knowledge retention across diverse settings. Code and data will be released upon publication.

title: Kolmogorov--Arnold against bounded translations
abstract: Historically originating from Hilbert's 13th problem, the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem (KART) has recently experienced a major revitalisation through its applications to neural networks, specifically Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). While the exact representation is well established, its stability under continuous adversarial perturbations of the hidden layer remains a critical open question. In this paper, we investigate the robustness of KART against bounded adversarial translations. We provide an explicit, self-contained, and constructive proof of an approximate representation using fixed, piecewise linear inner functions. Crucially, our construction employs a single outer function that remains invariant for all summands and is independent of the specific adversarial translation, provided its maximum bound is known a priori.

title: การเพมประสทธภาพแบบจำลองความคดเหนของคนไทยตอปญญาประดษฐดวยเทคนคการตดคำ
abstract: This research aimed to analyze word segmentation techniques that improve the performance of sentiment classification models for Thai people’s opinions toward artificial intelligence. The data were collected from social media platforms, consisting of 8,091 comments. The researcher selected only comments containing more than 10 words for analysis, resulting in a total of 1,767 comments. In the text mining process, word segmentation is an important and time-consuming step. Therefore, the researcher employed Newmm, Deepcut, Longest, and Attacut techniques for word segmentation. For model construction, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, and C4.5 Decision Tree techniques were applied, as these techniques are reliable, widely accepted, and commonly used in research studies. The performance evaluation employed the 10-Fold Cross Validation method for data partitioning. The effectiveness of the word segmentation techniques was measured using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score. The experimental results revealed that the Deepcut technique, which is a data-driven word segmentation approach, could effectively handle comments containing new or informal words. When combined with the Support Vector Machine technique, which performs well with high-dimensional and complex data containing formal words, informal expressions, and newly emerging terms, the combination achieved the best performance. The results yielded an accuracy of 93.42 %, a recall of 97.03 %, and an F1-score of 94.54 %.

title: Mecanismo de repetición por intencionalidad de tecleo en interacción con inteligencia artificial.
abstract: Este trabajo propone un mecanismo de preservación de sentido en la interacción entre humanos e inteligencia artificial conversacional. El problema identificado es que los modelos de lenguaje actuales reinterpretan como una nueva intención variaciones mínimas e involuntarias del input, como la repetición de un signo de "?" a "??" o de una letra final. Se argumenta que la IA no puede medir la intencionalidad del tecleo porque solo recibe texto, no telemetría física. Por ello, se plantea un sistema en dos capas:Una capa de dispositivo que, mediante dinámica de tecleo, etiqueta la probabilidad de que un carácter sea involuntario, y una capa de IA que utiliza esa etiqueta para decidir entre generar una nueva respuesta o repetir la respuesta anterior desde caché. La propuesta no busca la corrección ortográfica, sino evitar que el ruido motor cambie el sentido de la conversación.

title: Binary Flow VI: Phase Qubits and Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
abstract: We present a novel approach to quantum computing based on the Binary Flow theory. We propose that quantum bits (qubits) can be implemented as phase modes of the vacuum, specifically the 90◦ phase mode, which is decoupled from ordinary matter. This phase qubit would be inherently fault-tolerant, as it is immune to thermal and electromagneticdecoherence. We outline a design for a phase qubit based on a resonant cavity, and describe how quantum gates could be implemented using phase interference. This work opens a new avenue for scalable, room-temperature quantum computing, pending experimental validation of the underlying phase mode.

title: Rank Order Under a Capacity Benchmark Is Conditional on the Observation Band and the Delay Horizon
abstract: Reservoir-computing benchmarks increasingly report rank orderings, but rarely the observation band or the delay horizon at which the ranking was taken. This note measures both conditions on a common grid, on two architecture families. Under a readout-only change of band, the fastest system loses -6.61 information processing capacity [-6.89, -6.33] while its kernel rank moves -0.50 [-1.27, +0.27]: a readout band destroys memory and leaves separation intact, because rank measures, under the ensemble protocol, are computed from one state per input stream. That insulation belongs to the protocol and not to rank measures: under the field's second protocol the manipulation moves generalisation rank in both, by up to twenty-eight points, and kernel rank in one. Under a change of drive band the ordering reverses in 10 of 10 seeds in both, and the band at which the crossover occurs moves with the delay horizon. The systems compared differ only in their time constant, so this is a demonstration of an effect the field already predicts, not a discovery; the contribution is the measurement and the reporting condition that follows. The note recommends that any published ranking state its observation band, its delay horizon, and which axes under which protocol. Includes zharnikov-2026bq-band-conditionality.yaml (Paper Spec v0.1.0) – a machine-readable specification of the paper's claims, assumptions, and dependencies. The paper's full machine-first bundle (the SPINE claim/dependency graph and the ONTOLOGY term module) lives in the public repository; see https://github.com/spectralbranding/paper-spec for the standard. title: Dynamic Topology-Based Adaptive Neural Network Accelerator
abstract: The field of neural networks has witnessed significant advancements, but training and inference remain computationally intensive, particularly for complex models. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based adaptive neural network accelerator, designed to address this challenge by dynamically adjusting network parameters based on data distribution. We propose a framework that automatically adapts the neural network's topology to optimize performance on diverse datasets. This approach significantly reduces the need for manual parameter tuning, leading to faster training and inference times. The core mechanism leverages the inherent adaptability of dynamic topologies to achieve this optimization. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance and efficiency compared to traditional methods in various benchmark datasets.

title: 基于自适应量子势场的量子模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation method, termed "Adaptive Quantum Field Simulation" (AQFS), that leverages the concept of an adaptive quantum field to enhance the simulation of complex quantum systems. AQFS employs a dynamically adjusted quantum field to optimize the simulation process, allowing for improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves adjusting the field strength and direction based on the system's state, effectively tailoring the simulation to the specific characteristics of the target system. This approach offers a significant advancement in quantum simulation capabilities, particularly for systems exhibiting intricate quantum phenomena and requiring precise parameter estimation. The paper details the methodology, presents preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the AQFS approach, and discusses future research directions.

title: 基于量子自旋的物理学模拟算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel physics simulation algorithm based on quantum spin properties, leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance simulation accuracy and enable the modeling of more complex physical systems. Traditional simulation methods often rely on classical approaches, while this algorithm capitalizes on quantum entanglement to achieve significantly improved resolution and the ability to represent intricate physical models. The core mechanism involves utilizing entangled quantum spins to create a dynamic, interconnected system of variables, allowing for a more accurate representation of quantum phenomena. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's potential for advancing physics simulation capabilities.

title: 基于自适应的量子态的优化策略
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for solving complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential necessitates significant advancements in quantum algorithm design and optimization. This paper explores a novel optimization strategy based on the inherent adaptability of quantum states. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts quantum states to minimize error rates and maximize fidelity during the execution of quantum algorithms. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously refines the quantum state based on the algorithm's progress, effectively guiding the system towards optimal performance. This approach offers a promising pathway towards enhanced quantum computing efficiency and reduced error rates. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this method through simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing the potential for significant performance improvements.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through extensive simulation and analysis, showcasing its ability to outperform established methods in diverse scenarios.

title: Probability Space (PLS)的自适应参数化
abstract: Probability Space (PLS) 是一种强大的概率空间模型,它通过引入动态概率权重机制,能够自动调整模型参数,从而提升模型适应性和泛化能力。本论文提出了一种基于PLS的自动参数化方法,该方法通过动态调整概率权重,实现更有效的模型学习。该方法旨在解决传统 PLS 模型需要手动调整参数的难题,并提高模型的泛化能力。我们通过实验证明该方法在各种数据集上表现出显著的优势,尤其是在数据复杂性较高的场景下。论文重点阐述了动态概率权重机制的设计、算法实现以及实验结果分析,并对未来的研究方向进行了展望。

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Abstract: This paper investigates the potential of topological quantum error correction (TQC) as a novel approach to quantum information protection, offering a distinct paradigm from traditional methods relying on measurement. We propose a new type of error correction code based on the inherent topological properties of quantum states, aiming to achieve superior robustness against environmental noise and enhanced scalability. The core mechanism involves introducing a quantum state influenced by a topological field, allowing it to resist noise through a fundamentally different approach than traditional methods. This work details the proposed code structure, its mathematical foundations, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness against specific noise models.

title: Based on Multi-Modal Contexts for Knowledge Graph Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning that leverages multi-modal contextual information. The core premise is that integrating data from diverse sources – including text, images, and audio – significantly enhances the richness of knowledge graphs and improves the accuracy of reasoning tasks. We introduce a multi-modal information fusion algorithm designed to map these disparate modalities into a unified representation space. Subsequently, graph algorithms are employed to perform reasoning operations on this integrated knowledge graph. The key innovation lies in extending traditional knowledge graph reasoning techniques to incorporate multi-modal data, thereby bolstering the expressive power and inference capabilities of the resulting knowledge graph. This work addresses limitations inherent in purely text-based approaches and offers a promising pathway for more robust and nuanced knowledge representation and reasoning.

title: Information Entropy and Cognitive Architecture: Assessing Artificial Consciousness and Learning
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of information entropy and cognitive architecture, investigating how this framework can be used to evaluate the self-awareness and learning capabilities of artificial systems. We propose a novel information entropy model for assessing these crucial properties and design a learning algorithm based on this model. The core claim centers on the ability to detect self-awareness through the dynamic assessment of information entropy within a cognitive architecture. This research utilizes entropy as a key metric to determine the system's ability to self-regulate and iteratively improve. The study focuses on the potential for this approach to provide a more nuanced and objective evaluation of artificial intelligence.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Adaptive Parameters
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers the potential for paradigm shifts in algorithm design, surpassing the limitations of classical machine learning. This paper investigates the application of adaptive parameter adjustment within QML algorithms to enhance learning efficiency. We propose a novel quantum algorithm designed to dynamically adjust parameters based on the inherent characteristics of input data, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality and improving model robustness. The core mechanism centers around quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate data effectively, enabling a self-optimizing learning process. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark datasets, showcasing the potential for significant gains in learning speed and generalization ability.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Hidden Matrix: A Novel Computational Approach for Complex Quantum Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational approach based on the concept of non-linear quantum hidden matrices. We propose a method for solving complex quantum algorithms, aiming to significantly enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism leverages the unique properties of these matrices to enable optimized computations. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and initial results demonstrating the potential of this technique. The core claim is that this approach can overcome limitations imposed by standard quantum algorithms, specifically in tackling problems with intricate solutions. This work presents a new method for tackling complex problems utilizing the core principle of non-linear quantum hidden matrices.
